utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You'll now be cross-examined by counsel for the various accused, and before starting I'll just check the order in which they will do that. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will follow the indictment, with one change, counsel for General Pavkovic will go last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, the first counsel to cross-examine you, Mr. Cvetic, Mr. O'Sullivan. Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: My name is Toma Fila; I appear on behalf of Mr. Sainovic. I will have a few questions for you, and I hope we can deal with them quickly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The first thing that interests me is how come you gave your statement in 2004? Were you summoned, called to give it, or did it happen in some other way?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd of January, 2004, members of the Ministry of the Interior from Belgrade, I don't know from which administration they came, came to my house in Kragujevac. They issued me with a summons and with two decisions, or rather, waivers by which I was relieved of keeping state and official secrets.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you attended the interview, you were interviewed by two persons, as far as I can see, a man and a woman, Annette Murtagh and Philip Coo. My question is this: How did they introduce themselves?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They introduced themselves as investigators of The Hague Tribunal, and they said that they wanted to speak with me on certain topics which had been given to me by the MUP inspectors.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. We are speaking the same language, so I need to pause. Therefore, I can conclude that you spoke with both, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Another thing that I'd like to know is this: At a certain point in time, you decided to testify using your full first and last name without any protective measures. When did you make that decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a long internal dialogue. I was unsure whether I should make use of protective measures or to testify in open session. It was a great dilemma for me because at that point in time I was in serious and grave situation. The decision was a hard one, and I made it at the last moment when I came here just before testifying.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement and in your examination-in-chief, you described the way the MUP was organised and functioned. I will have a few questions on that topic pertaining to 1998. I will clarify further. In your statement, there is a mention of 1996 and then 1999 and then 1998. We know our way about it since we are from the same area, but this is an international tribunal; therefore, I wanted to be quite clear as to what year I will be referring to. The question is this: First of all, in 1998 can you confirm to us that the chain of command, as envisaged by the law on internal affairs, was operational throughout 1998, it was in place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the chain of command within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you were a policeman.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The next question may appear strange, but some people testified here about it; therefore, it is not something I invented. The report that you -- or the reports you sent to Belgrade as the head of the SUP, and you also copied those reports for the MUP staff, did I understand it correctly?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the same report. It would be the same report sent to the MUP staff and to Belgrade. It included the most important events of security interest in the past 24 hours. Such reports were forwarded to the MUP staff and to the duty operations centre of the MUP in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone work on your reports additionally once you drafted them in order to show the situation in a different manner, to make the worse more plausible?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one meddled with my reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did Nikola Sainovic meddle with your reports?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I have a question about the way the VJ was organised. Of course you're not familiar with it as well as with the MUP, but according to your knowledge, do you know whether the VJ in 1998 also followed its chain command as envisaged by the law?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did you know that the 3rd Army, the part of which was the Pristina Corps, had a forward command post in Pristina and General Samardzic was there in 1998? It's still 1998.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that. I know that the command of the 3rd Army was in Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Fine. Let us move on. I wanted to ask you something of importance for us, so as to be able to establish the background to the events from the indictment. The Prosecutor did not find it necessary to ask you this, hence I'm asking you. In 1996 and 1997, you as the head of SUP, you noticed there was a certain person by the name of Jashari. For that person, you said that he was a commander of a terrorist group. You also said that they interrupted road communication in Drenica, and that you spoke about that with Minister Stojiljkovic. I just wanted to remind you, although I know you remember it quite well. I'm interested in this: What was the reaction on the part of the people, the people from that area, as Jashari's actions were concerned and the terrorism being introduced into the area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of December, 1996, when I was sent to Kosovska Mitrovica to be the head of SUP, I learned from my chiefs of OUP and commanders of police stations as to what the situation was and what the problems were in their area. The basic problem they all mentioned was the issue of terrorism, especially in Srbica. The head of OUP in Srbica and the commander of the police station there stressed that issue. So that I could gain more detail and insight, I was sent by the head of the public security department to see a person by the name of Jovic. I can't recall his first name. He was the chief of the operations group tasked with identifying people engaging in terrorist activities in Kosovo. He forwarded the list of such people, and the list comprised 21 persons. The group was headed by Adem Jashari. I went through the entire file that was at the disposal of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP. On that occasion, I learned that that specific group, as of 1991, conducted a number of activities in that area, and that on the 30th of December, 1991, the police from the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP and the MUP staff from Pristina attempted to arrest Adem Jashari. There was quite a resistance put up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I have to interrupt you. We don't have time for 1991 in this trial. The question you were asked was about the reaction on the part of people, the people from the area, as far as Jashari's actions were concerned and the terrorism being introduced into the area. Now, could you bring it much nearer to the time of the conflict, please, the reaction at the time you went rather than what was happening in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In 1996 and 1997, the road communication was interrupted and you mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it seems the witness is not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: A road was blocked, and you mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1996 and in 1997, a road was blocked, the main road between Kosovska Mitrovica and Pec, which went via Klina and Rudnik as well as Rakos. That road at the time could not be used, as barricades were put up. The police at the police station in Srbica and the citizens employed with the municipal authorities could not go to work using buses, because they were afraid that the terrorist groups from that area may conduct an operation, and the group was headed by Jashari. There was a great reaction on the part of the people from Srbica, and particularly from the two Serb villages of Suvo Grlo and Banje. They couldn't use the road to go to Kosovska Mitrovica; they had to go the round about way via Zubin Potok to reach Kosovska Mitrovica. There was a reaction on the part of the people and the municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did the Albanian citizens react against the abductions and theft conducted by those people?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the loyal Albanians did react.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you clarify, who principally were the people who reacted to the roadblock?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The people employed with the municipal state authorities as well as those employed at the police station. In Srbica, the only thing that was functioning at the time was the municipality. Other companies were not operational at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You said that there was a great reaction on the part of the people from Srbica, and you said particularly from the two Serb villages of Suvo Grlo and Banje and there's something missing. Now, are you essentially saying that the reaction against the roadblock was by the Serb population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. -- thank you. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But not only on their part. The loyal Albanians joined in too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us move on. I apologise for possibly having interrupted Your Honour. Let us move on to more specific issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: During your examination-in-chief, you described the meeting in July 1998 when you were advised on the formation of the Joint Command. You said that their role was to coordinate activities between the VJ and the MUP. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If I could also ask you, you've given evidence already that the normal chain of command, according to the law of the interior, was in place for both the MUP and the VJ throughout 1998. Now, the Joint Command you've told us earlier had been established by July 1998. Are you saying that with it in place, the normal chains of command continued to operate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something of great importance. Your memory seems to be excellent. Can you mention -- can you remember whether Obrad, the general, told you about the establishment of the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, 1998, I cannot recall whether I was told that by Obrad Stevanovic or Rodja Djordjevic. However, on the 22nd of July - and I remember this well - that Rodja Djordjevic conveyed to us that the command had been established at the highest level.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I'm sorry I cannot jog your memory any further. Can you recall who told you about the composition of this coordination body, as I would call it, and you are calling it the Joint Command. Who told you about its composition? I have in mind Milomir Minic and Sainovic and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 22nd of July at the MUP staff meeting, this was conveyed by Rodja Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Earlier you told us that coordination was needed between the Army of Yugoslavia and the MUP. Earlier, yesterday during the examination-in-chief you said that certain civilians had some assignments, such as Matkovic for the economy and so on and so forth. What I would like to find out from you is the following: If coordination was required between the army and the MUP, what was Dusan Matkovic doing there with the economy? Was this a little bit broader than just military and police coordination? Was there a political aspect to this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Joint Command had certain persons who were charged with certain things. Just like in any military command, there were assignments for certain sectors. Matkovic was entrusted with the economy and economic activities, whereas Mr. Nikola Sainovic was entrusted with the coordination between the military and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What about Andjelkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time Andjelkovic was acting president of the temporary Executive Council, and then after the 28th of September Assembly session, he became the president of the TEC.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What were his duties at the command, though? If you don't know, fine.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: What I would like to get from you, if possible, is: This Joint Command, I'm still going to refer to it as coordination, but it's Joint Command, there is the military aspect, the police aspect, but there is some other matters also; for example, the economy and so on. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mentioned Milomir Minic. You said that he had an important function in the SPS and was an important political figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need to have in the transcript besides the military, the police aspect, and the economic aspect, the political aspect as well. That is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could you please say yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You mentioned Milomir Minic. You said that he was a high MUP official, high-ranking SPS official, and that he was something in the Federal Assembly. If I were to tell you that he was the president of the Federal Assembly, would you take my word for it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that he was the president of one of the chambers of the Federal Assembly but which one --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right, all right, very well, all right.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I am wrong. I think that he was the chairman of one of the chambers of the Federal Assembly, because at the time the Assembly had the chamber of the citizens and the chamber of the republic, so I don't know which one it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well. You also said that Matkovic -- the chamber of citizens. You said that Matkovic was one of the vice-presidents. I think that there were five of them. Sorry, not Matkovic, Sainovic. I'm beginning to suffer from age. I don't get younger every year; I get older. So Sainovic was one of the deputy prime ministers in the federal government. Since we know that the president of the chamber of citizens in the Federal Assembly is person number two, he becomes the person in charge if something should happen to the president. So who had higher rank, according to you, Milos Minic or Nikola Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about two branches of government, the legislative and the executive government. The legislative government or branch is higher than the executive government, because the legislative branch enacts laws and the executive branch implements those laws.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, could you repeat that question, please, because you were talking over the translation of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The question is: According to the Yugoslav constitution, which was in force until a few days ago, the president of the Assembly has a higher rank than a deputy prime minister. Isn't that so? He can stand in for the president of the republic, for example.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Assembly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe the witness can offer an opinion but isn't that really a legal question, a question of legal interpretation of the constitution at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, let's -- I think this witness can answer that question, if he feels he has the knowledge. It's a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Federal Assembly had its president, the president of the Federal Assembly, and there were two president of the chambers of the Federal Assembly, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Very well. We'll move on. Do you believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've also to remember the concept that existed in Yugoslavia, that it wasn't so much rank that mattered, it was the office that you held. You'll remember the evidence in relation to some of the positions that the ranks that people have held. I think in relation to the investigation into Batajnica and the refrigerated lorry we learned that. So perhaps it's not quite simply a matter of rank in the political arena either, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about (redacted), because rank in our MUP is also linked to the level of education. Doctorate -- a person with a doctorate could have been a minister, if they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you think that because of that, perhaps it would be more logical that Milomir Minic would have a higher rank than Sainovic in this coordination, especially because you saw some reports presented to you by the Prosecutor, who opens the meetings, who makes the conclusions, and so on. Wouldn't that be more logical in your view?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is your answer yes or ...

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Federal Assembly, the Assembly that includes both chambers, in order for the Assembly, in order for the decisions of the Federal Assembly to be important and to be adopted, both chambers had to adopt those decisions. If they were adopted only at the session of one chamber, they could not be applied.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've got the same problem, Mr. Fila. You're going to have to repeat all that because you've been talking over the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The president of the Federal Chamber chairs the Assembly when laws are being enacted that have to be passed by both chambers. That's how it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Fila, we've exhausted the potential knowledge of the witness on this. Let's move to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: You told us that you did not attend any meetings of this Joint Command, and now what I'm interested in is the following. Did you find out anywhere how it was holding its meetings, where were they convened, who was chairing the meetings, and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any information about that. I don't know where they were physically located.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. You said -- you spoke --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Stop a moment. Wasn't the evidence yesterday that the witness did not attend any meetings of the Joint Command? You may be right. Sorry. Please carry on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Something wasn't articulated, so perhaps you will correct me if I misunderstood. Speaking about this you said that in 1999 you saw several orders by the Joint Command, and based on that I understood that in 1998 you didn't see any such orders. If I understood you correctly. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we will move to 1999, these are the meetings of the MUP staff where you were, and you said that the army did not participate in these meetings from the 24th of March until the 16th of September, 1999.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP staff meetings in the period from the 24th of March to the 16th of April, military representatives were not attending these meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: When they were present in 1999, you said that there were maps on the desks, and that Lukic and Pavkovic spoke, if I understood you correctly --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I suspect that there might be a problem, at least for the record, if counsel doesn't indicate that when he refers to what the witness said, I think it is something he said in his statement, not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I certainly don't remember this evidence, so it can't be in the evidence from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct, in the statement. All right. Then we will ask him like this:

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The meetings before this period that we mentioned just a little bit before, the meetings that were attended by representatives of the Army of Yugoslavia, were there any maps at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, before the anti-terrorist activities began to be implemented, and this was on the 25th of July, 1998, so this was before the 25th of July, at a meeting in the MUP headquarters there were representatives of the military and there were topographical military maps 1:50.000 ratio, and in those maps the forces and the equipment were drawn in and also the axes were established at which the military and police units were to operate. And as for when the action was going to start --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I just wanted to indicate the difference between 1998 and 1999. Now we will move to the 4th of April, 1999; that's the meeting you mentioned that Sainovic appeared at. From the minutes it can be seen -- this is an exhibit by the Defence, so, if necessary, we are going to bring it up. At the end of the minutes it's mentioned -- or Sainovic appears. He's not in the earlier part when the -- those present are being noted and so on. So can I conclude on the basis of that that he wasn't at the meeting from the beginning but that he joined the meeting towards the end, or should I show you those minutes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very well. How could I not? That meeting was attended from the beginning by Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The minutes seem to indicate something else, but never mind. Do you know why he came? He's not -- he's not in the minutes. Let's look at the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is Exhibit number 1998 -- P1989. Please look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you see page 1, first of all, and you can see who is mentioned as being in attendance. It doesn't mention Nikola Sainovic anywhere. Now, please look at page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, please. I'm sorry, can we look at page 4. Can we look at page 4 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: And based on what it says, it says that he joined the work and that he wasn't there right from the beginning, so perhaps your recollection of this meeting is not quite correct --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There is a translation issue. The English translation we have is just he joined the work --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- not that he was not there from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. This is a matter of interpretation. Mr. Cvetic, there is a paragraph of five lines after the bullet points, the first paragraph after these bullet points. Could you read the first line of that paragraph to us aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The federal deputy prime minister, Mr. Nikola Sainovic, joined the work."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: But you see that he's not mentioned in the list of those attending, but that he joined --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is the list of those attending? It gives a list of people reporting or what they did, but is there a list of people attending?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, can we look at page 1 of this same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you please kindly read the sentence beginning: "The meeting was held," and then read it till the end.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The meeting was held by Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic and Major-General Sreten Lukic, and it was attended by the chiefs of all the secretariats, commands, detachments of the PJP, commander of the SAJ, and commander JSO, RDB." The name Nikola Sainovic is not referred to here, but I remember that Nikola Sainovic did attend the meeting and joined the discussion after all of the prior discussions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just -- again, just a moment. Is General Lukic or General Stevanovic referred to in the first page of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, they don't appear in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the translation is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's a heck of a mistake to make in the translation. That's one that will definitely need to be invested.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It seems now that the translation, the official translation, is erroneous and that is one I worked at. But I now have been told that there is a draft translation which has that in it, strangely enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could we have the first page in the English, please, on the screen. Thank you. Now, what are you saying, Mr. Stamp? This is said to be an English translation. It doesn't say it's a draft.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no. The -- strangely, as it would sound, the formal official translation has made an error, I now realise, and that is what I was working from. However, I have also just discovered that there was a draft translation which contains the quotation that was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm quite -- I'm quite concerned about it, because I can see three numbers, 1, 2, and 3 on the Serb version, and they don't appear in the English translation either. This requires investigation. Please carry on, Mr. Fila, and I will take the matter up with CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, it is not in dispute that Mr. Sainovic was there. What is in question is the moment he arrived, and another thing that is not in dispute is the words ascribed to him in the minutes. I'm just stating that he joined the meeting later. As you can see from the fourth page -- maybe I can read it out to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've dealt with this, Mr. Fila. The witness has given you as definite an answer as anyone could ever give about anything, and he's clear that Mr. Sainovic was there at the beginning, so let's move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Would you allow for a possibility that on that day some officers were promoted and that he had been invited to attend and address those present?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The last sentence says: "Those promoted were handed out certificates." Please have a look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 4 of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Wait a few seconds. The last sentence, "the extraordinarily promoted," please read it out.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The extraordinarily promoted commanding officers have been issued decisions on their appointments to higher ranks."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Could it have been that he was invited to attend to address those present, as Mr. Sainovic claims was the reason?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the reason was, but I know what Mr. Sainovic said at the meeting and I mentioned it specifically yesterday. I can repeat if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That is not in dispute. Let us conclude with this document. Do you think it was a speech of a high political official who came there to boost morale, it was just prior to the NATO attacks, and he came to see a group of people who were patriots fighting for their country and trying to boost their morale. Can we say that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrival of all those politicians who attended, and inviting certain military officers to attend a political meeting, well, if we put that in that context, then, yes, we could see it as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. The other meeting you mentioned where you said he didn't participate but he only followed agency reports, I -- it must have been quite a large meeting room for you to be able to convene your meeting at one end and for him to be able to watch the TV at the other?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the basement of the Grand Hotel, we were a bit further away, separated from him, and in another part he was following agency reports, foreign agencies' reports, about the NATO bombing in Yugoslavia and the reactions it caused.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Therefore, he wasn't present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said he was there but that he did not participate in the meeting itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvetic. Let us move on. You spoke about the period of the so-called fight against terrorism. Did you know that in Belgrade there was an interministerial staff that was organised to counter terrorism?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who headed that staff, what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the formation of this interministerial staff, I can tell you the following: In March or April 1998, I think in April 1998, the interministerial staff to fight terrorism was established. What does it mean, "interministerial"? It meant that the functions of the state and the public security department were brought together. The head of the staff was Mr. Jovica Stanisic, who was at the time the head of the state security department. His deputy was Rodja Djordjevic, who was the head of the public security department. In that staff, apart from the head and his deputy, there were also David Gajic, Obrad Stevanovic, Loncar from the state security department, and Radomir Markovic, as well as Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did they issue any orders for operations in Kosovo while the staff was in existence until October 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Interministerial staff drafted an action plan for the units of both state and public security in fighting terrorism, and the plan was in existence at the time in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P1968. I believe we saw it yesterday. It has to do with the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I would kindly ask for brief answers. I'm having less and less time, both in this cross-examination and in my life in general.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't sum it up in one sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: In this document before you, would you agree with me that it is a military document, not a police one, but a military one. It says: "Order to provide support to MUP." Is it so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is this a military document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Or a police one?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a military document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us move on to the next page, item 4. Item 4. It says: "Decision." Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Please read out the first two words or the first line.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I have decided to support MUP forces in the attack by engaging main forces on the following axis."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Who decided? The commander of the Pristina Corps. Does it come from the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see the whole document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: This is it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, what about the signature block?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That's the problem, there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: If you go on reading it, you'll see for yourself. And then the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One more page, all the way to the end. More. Just leaf through. One more page. One more. Yes. Here's the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: No signature, as you can see.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it says "Joint Command."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is this a document from the Pristina Corps or not, or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Judging by this, it seems that the Pristina Corps drafted this document and it was verified at the Joint Command meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, this document comes from the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: It also says: "Joint Command."

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nevertheless, I want to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us please see it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it states "Joint Command."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The person who decided was not the Joint Command, but a commander, the commander of the Pristina Corps, I guess?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the body of the Joint Command, as in any other military command, there are certain methods of work. A command representative, in this specific case the commander of the Pristina Corps, can draft something and submit it to the Joint Command for verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Now I understand, and this was by way of introduction.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Well, you saw that document already. It is a Prosecution exhibit with the call signals, I believe. 1052. Mr. Cvetic, it says here "Joint Command" in the left-hand corner, upper left-hand corner. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: To the right it says "call signal Pastrik."

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Is it possible that throughout your career you haven't heard of this call signal, Pastrik, as being the call signal for the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. This concludes my cross-examination. You don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Fila. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvetic, my name is Mihajlo Bakrac; I appear for General Lazarevic. I will have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I wanted to clarify some things. Yesterday you were examined by my learned friend Mr. Stamp. He asked you about the work of the military war courts and military prosecutors. You mentioned the 4th of April as the date when they were meant to start functioning. Would I be able to jog your memory that by a decree of the 21st of March -- of the 27th of March, the decree by the president of the republic, the military war courts and military prosecutors were being established?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the regular courts or about the wartime military courts?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I mean the wartime military courts and wartime military prosecutors.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that. We haven't received a single document about it, no notification. The meeting discussed the beginning of the work of such bodies, and until that point in time all reports were to be sent to the regular courts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. During your examination-in-chief, when asked by Mr. Stamp, you spoke about reserve police squads, the RPOs. You said that some units from the military departments, when not engaged otherwise, could be made part of these RPOs. Would you agree with me that it would be more correct to say that individual recruits with the war assignment in the VJ, upon MUP's request, could have been deployed elsewhere. Their war assignment could have been changed, provided they were made part of the civilian protection or the RPOs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Their war assignment was not changed whatsoever. That's how they were introduced into RPOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, some people had their war assignments changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I have only one more question. Would you agree with me if I said that it is correct that the police was never resubordinated to the army?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in Kosovo until the 16th, the units and bodies of the Ministry of the Interior were not subordinated to the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My name is Branko Lukic, and unfortunately I will have a bit more questions for you than my learned friends. I kindly ask for your assistance so as to be able to clarify some things from the domain of your testimony and work. I will start with a general question. You told us that you being sent to Kosovo was something you saw as a demotion. What about other cases of people being sent to Kosovo, was that also demotion, a demotion when it comes to policemen and police officials?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know about other cases. I just stated my view of that transfer, or rather, that was based on the method of my superiors, the method they used against me. It was inhumane and unprofessional.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could a policeman refuse to go to Kosovo, and what would happen in that case?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such cases as well. The policemen who refused to go to Kosovo were fired, but after the 5th of October, 2001, all those policemen who had been removed or fired for refusing to go to Kosovo were reinstated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Is it correct that the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, which you headed, could not ensure the freedom of movement and the protection of citizens and property with their own resources, so you asked from Minister Stojiljkovic, General Djordjevic and Ilic for the MUP to enable freedom of movement, especially in the Srbica-Pec direction?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that there were attacks, kidnappings, roads were blocked, police patrols were attacked and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year was this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that this was in 1997. Did the same apply to early 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just stop a moment. Line 1 of page 27, the answer given was "yes" and should be reflected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please carry on now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvetic, I am going to make pauses, not because I'm dissatisfied with your replies but because we are speaking the same language. I would also like to tell you if there is something you don't know, feel free to say so. That is also a legitimate response. Please don't feel that you have to tell me whatever I am asking you. The Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, did it have information and have sufficient indications pointing to the perpetrators of criminal acts that were committed by the members of the KLA at the time? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean terrorist crimes?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Is it true that you didn't have the strength to prevent these things being committed or to arrest the perpetrators, you and the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the time we were not allowed to take steps unless there was agreement from a higher level to take part in these actions. Specifically, I am referring to this question that you put when I -- when Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic and Vlajkovic [as interpreted] when they were at the meeting at the MUP headquarters on the 27th of May, 1997, and when I made this request to them this was not allowed at the time, and what was said was that no local police members, because there was a reaction by the local police, they wanted to take these measures by themselves, that they should not take any measures on their own until they received instructions to do that. Later, there was another meeting with Mr. Stojiljkovic and he said that this problem is something that the leadership of the country was informed about and that no one is to take any steps unless this was first decided upon by the top leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In early 1991 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Early 1999 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- you, as the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, did you have enough resources to combat terrorism?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No activity could have been carried out without the approval of the headquarters and their agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Could you please tell us what the powers and the duties of the SUP are for the territory where they are established.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SUP work is regulated by the Law on Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please briefly tell us the main points of that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Briefly said, it's the protection of personal property and security and combatting all forms of crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As the SUP chief, who were you responsible to for the security situation as well as for the work and the functioning of the SUP and its units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was responsible to the minister in any event, to the chief of the department, the headquarters chief, and also to the chiefs of individual administrations within the ministry entrusted with certain sectors; for example, for police matters to the police chief, for the crimes, I was responsible to the crimes chief, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You said that on the 11th of June, 1998, Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic appointed General-Major Sreten Lukic to head the headquarters in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that. I didn't say that Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic appointed him. I said that the -- that Lukic was appointed to this position according to an order by the sector chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was that a regular substitute for the previous person who was carrying out that assignment for a year?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his question. He's reading too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you're not pausing and you're going too quickly, say the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'll repeat my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You see, we've missed another answer, and I think the answer was "yes" again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In line 22, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By appointing Sreten Lukic as the chief of the staff, were there any changes in the organisation of work to date and the authorities and the powers of the SUPs, compared to the previous period?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the organisation of the work of the SUPs?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the SUPs.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Also, none of the regulations guiding the work of MUP was not changed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The regulations of the MUP were the same other than this decision. Nowhere was it mentioned -- nowhere was the Pristina MUP staff mentioned, other than the decision on its establishment. I never encountered that in any other regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who comprised the headquarters before the start of the NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP staff, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Who do you remember being there.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the starting of the bombing? How long before? A day? Two days? Three days?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In March 1999.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In March 1999, the staff included Mr. Sreten Lukic, who was the Chief of Staff; Mijatovic was the deputy Chief of Staff; Dusko Adamovic; Goran Radosavljevic; Mr. Novica Zdravkovic; Vukovic; Zarko Brakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I didn't expect so many names, that you would recall all those names after so much time has passed. Thank you. And now a question that might be strange to you, but we found it in the papers. You as a member of the -- or you as the chief of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, were you a member of the MUP Pristina staff also?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally, by first and last name, no; but in the decision on the establishment of the staff, it is stated that the chiefs of the SUPs are part of the broader composition of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So even though it is stated in the decision, you were not a member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You asked me whether I, Ljubinko Cvetic, was a member of the staff, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Thank you. Is it correct that all SUPs, including those in Kosovo and Metohija were obliged to send a report every day to the MUP on the security situation in the territory, and that this was in force before 1998 also. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The security situation, no, but about the events and incidents, yes. There is a big difference between those two terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there are laymen here who do not understand all the fine distinctions of your profession, but thank you in any case. Is it correct that in extraordinary situations, the first report would be submitted by telephone?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that after that there would be a dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the communication within the MUP in the territory of the entire republic, a special telephone network called "specijal" was used, you mentioned that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall how many "specijals" there were in your SUP staff and who had this kind of line available?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the SUP, the deputy chief of SUP, the chief of the police sector, the OUP, the crime-fighting department chief, the chief of the department for general and joint affairs. This would be at the seat of the secretariat. Out of the secretariat seat, there was such a line in Leposavic, in Srbica, these are the OUP chiefs, and also the OUP chief in Vucitrn.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And also the emergency duty service had that as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we assume, then, that this was not some super secret kind of telephone line, that these were regular telephone lines that were used within the SUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those lines were part of the PTT system but they were more protected or more secure than the regular lines in the PTT. They did not provide 100 per cent security, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Thank you. During bombing, did you use the "specijal" lines, and what were the connections like, let's say, after the 24th or the 25th of March when the bombing started?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the bombing started, we were using the special lines. For as long as we used them until the PTT building in Pristina was destroyed by NATO bombing. Then again, special connections were organised, but once again these were communications at certain locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we confirm that the PTT building in Pristina was bombed on the 27th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember when the PTT building in Pristina was bombed, but I do recall that the MUP building where the staff was located was bombarded on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in that period. I cannot remember whether it was precisely on the 27th, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we agree -- I have an exhibit here but perhaps there is no need to show it. It's about reports being sent to Belgrade first. It was always sent to the Ministry of Internal Affairs Belgrade, as you said today, using a professional term DOC; that would be the emergency operation centre in Belgrade. And parallel to that, reports were also sent to the ministry staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit 6D129 on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, please, Mr. Cvetic, while the document is brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the heading of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I would like to ask you is whether it happened, as we can see on the basis of this document, that the MUP of Republic of Serbia informs and issues directions to the SUPs, all 33 of the secretariats, without informing the MUP staff in Kosovo first?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see that from this document, this is 6D129. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the number dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, this is the number of this document.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the dispatch of the crime police administration, and it's marked DD, which means very urgent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the bottom of the document so that we can see who actually signed this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chief of administration, Major-General Dragan Ilic. At the time, he was the chief of the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now bring up document P1090 on the e-court system, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before that happens, this is an intimation of a crime and a request for assistance in detaining suspects. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. All we wanted to show is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's hardly an order from the Ministry of the Interior in Belgrade for action by the SUPs. It's what you would expect any police force might issue worldwide, never mind to the area of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what we found in haste, trying to show this point, but the witness also confirmed that this situation happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But certainly this document wouldn't be much foundation for drawing from that that the orders for serious action on the part of the SUPs in Kosovo would come from Belgrade bypassing the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll have more time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've got the chance to ask the witness if you want, but that's a matter for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I wanted to ask you this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit P1092 put up on e-court. [In English] I think that we have a wrong document on the e-court. We need 1092. Actually, we'll skip that one. Can we see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've got it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see -- we have more documents. Obviously we have some problem with this one. Can we see 6D130, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have this document now, Mr. Cvetic. My next question is -- and it seems His Honour, Mr. Bonomy, is also interested in this aspect of the issue. It happened frequently that the public security department in sending their dispatches sent them to all the SUPs, all 33 of them, and at the same time to the MUP staff in Pristina. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And in the signature block we see?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see General Misic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this document show - and it is also the position of our Defence - that the staff was not a body which was to be found between the ministry and the SUPs, in the sense that the SUPs had to report to the staff and then the staff would decide who to report further. Is it correct that when SUPs were notified, they were notified on the same occasion or at the same time as the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, one cannot say that. Sometimes we received information without the knowledge of the staff. On other occasions, both instances were informed, and yet on some other ones only the staff would receive some information. What was your question actually?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D134 on e-court. While we're waiting for it to appear on the screen, I wanted to tell you that -- yes, here it is. It is a document dealing with disciplinary proceedings. We see here as well that the Ministry of the Interior and the SUP in Pristina -- well, it says the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia to the police administration, and it can be seen there that consent is sought to initiate disciplinary proceedings and adopt decisions on the removal of four employees of the given SUP. Is it correct that this document was not copied to the MUP staff in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct, and I believe in my opinion that the MUP staff did not have to be informed of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, Mr. Cvetic. Thank you. And what was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain it in detail. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, so as to move more quickly, is it correct that the MUP staff in Kosovo was not authorised to participate in any disciplinary proceedings undertaken against workers of the various SUPs in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was done by the secretariats, but the secretariats could not do anything on their own until they had received a consent of their superior administration within the MUP. They were the only ones who could give consent to a SUP for the SUP to be able to institute a proceedings, disciplinary proceedings against one of their workers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it is a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it is a good time, and we will break --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can continue with this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- in a second, but that answer didn't deal with the point very well, I don't think. It's not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Because it's, again, language problem. It's possible in our language to say no and continue with this kind of answer but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I -- it's not that that's the problem. It's they couldn't do it until they received a consent of their superior administration within the MUP. That doesn't answer the question where that superior administration was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The witness can explain that and then we can go to the break, if you want.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Could you explain that, please, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When discussing the ministry giving approval to institute proceedings, where is the seat of that ministry? Can you tell the Court.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we have to break, Mr. Cvetic. Could you again go with the usher, and we will see you again in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In fact, it will be half an hour in this case. It will be a longer break, so it will be at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Stamp, I gather you can deal with the translation problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If I may briefly with your leave, Mr. President. And particularly because I said something earlier which might indicate that the erroneous translation was the work of the CLSS. It was not. There was an error in the uploading, and the draft OTP internal translation was, in fact, the one uploaded, and that had been shown. We have corrected it and we have now placed instead the correct CLSS translation, which appears to be a correct translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. It's a great relief. And thank you for doing it timeously so that if anyone wishes to cross-examine on it, that can be done. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we continue, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 6D133 put on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we are having here a document concerning disciplinary proceedings. We will go back to the time of the war. We have here a dispatch drafted by the chief of the public security department, Mr. Radoljub Djordjevic, dated the 9th of April, 1999. Is it correct, first of all, that this document, inter alia, was sent to all the SUPs, then to the organisational units at the seat of the ministry, to the police college, as well as to the police high school, to the disciplinary court, and to the higher disciplinary court? Is it correct, as you had stated, that the staff had nothing to do with disciplinary proceedings and that it was not one of the addressees of this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it shouldn't be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Concerning this - and it may strike you as strange but I have to ask you this question because of the nature of proceedings here - I wanted to ask you whether the chief of the staff could institute a disciplinary proceedings against any member of the MUP in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have Exhibit P1251.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this on the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, it's not. If you have any questions regarding disciplinary proceedings, you can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I have one question, Mr. Cvetic. Assuming the chief of the MUP staff were to learn of conduct by MUP officers which amounted to murder, what action would you expect him to take in relation to these officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The chief of SUP, or a chief of SUP, once notified that any of the SUP members committed any crime, sends out a dispatch immediately to the ministry and the minister of the interior. He sends it to the competent administration within the ministry. This is what I'm trying to say. If this was a regular policeman, he addresses the police administration. If it was an operative, he forwards it to the crime administration, and he notifies the public security department chief, as well as seeks leave to take measures pursuant to the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be that my question was not properly translated to you. The question was: Assuming the chief of the MUP staff in Pristina, that's Mr. Lukic, were to learn of conduct by MUP officers which amounted to murder, what action would you expect him to take in relation to these officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He is to notify immediately the head of his organisational unit, that is the chief of the SUP, from which the policeman comes from. He is also to notify the chief of the public security department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I had the whole set of questions regarding different levels of SUP, but I thought that it's much faster to inquire whether a head of staff could process any police officer. So I think that this is consistent with my previous questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, it is, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvetic, before us is P1251, although you cannot see that number on your screen. It is a decision on the formation of a staff of the ministry in Pristina. The last paragraph on this page, it is difficult to see --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will do my utmost to try and read it, and we have the translation so the Bench and the OTP can try and follow. In item E it says -- first of all, under 1 at the top we have: "Notification on the formation of a staff." In item 2 the tasks are defined. And then the few or last words under item 2, which state that involved or that pertained to. In the last subitem, it involves training organised units to perform successfully special security assignments, and especially to maintain the readiness of secretariats and their organisational units. The PJP, the SAJ, the mechanised brigades of the police to implement the Kolubara 1 plan. Were these the -- or was this the authority given to the staff concerning the JSO, the SAJ, and the PJP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, just the SAJ and the PJP, not the JSO.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're not talking about command here but about training and exercising. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But when the unit is engaged, then the procedure is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We will come to that. Thank you. This is just in order to clarify. I don't know if it's a question of interpretation because yesterday something was in the transcript that I think was not said, so this is why I was seeking this clarification from you. Thank you. When we're dealing with the -- with the special police units, yesterday you said something, and is it true that these units had their own chain of command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me. I don't know which special units of the police you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let's see first. Yesterday we were talking about PJPs, that they are not special police units. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. They are not special police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the PJP had their own chain of command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever take part in 1999 in any action by the PJP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. How many PJP detachments did you have added to you during the state of war? I think that this did not go down in the transcript, so I would like you to now tell us the number of such units.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two detachments, the 35th and the 85th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Other than these detachments, you also had a PJP company made up of the employees of your SUP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the PJP company of the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP was part of the 124th Intervention Brigade. It was just actually the staff from the Kosovska Mitrovica SUP, but it was actually part of the forces of the 124th Intervention Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Is it correct that any other officers and members of the PJP had their own post and occasionally carried out assignments in the PJP when the unit was engaged?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes, but I cannot really say that for each individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Thank you. And what was the post of the commander of your PJP company in your SUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the police department. He was an inspector in the police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to move to the topic of the Joint Command. My learned friend Mr. Fila already put some questions to you about that, and I am also going to have a number of questions. First -- again, I would like to begin at your level, the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica chief. Did anything change at the SUP level in relation to your work and reporting with the forming of this body that we termed here the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please concentrate on the meeting of the 22nd of July, 1998. Do you recall - of course, if you recall - what the agenda of this meeting was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the precise words of the agenda, but the discussion at the meeting was on preparations to execute anti-terrorist actions, and I think it was one of the phases to bring, or rather, to have certain forces of the PJP brought in and deciding which of those forces should be brought to the area of Kosovo. That was one topic. The other topic were plans, when the action would begin, with which forces, which means would be utilised, and what the assignments would be of the units in that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the plans were already prepared when they were dealt with at that meeting. You had finished plans at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the action began?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 25th of July, on a Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it was just covered, then, at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just for the transcript I would like to confirm the following: You were never duty-bound to report to the Joint Command on anything?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the chief of the secretariat, the SUP?
